summary: Blue-limestone lighthouse on Lake Champlain at Westport, lit 1873 and automated 1935; now a private home in a National Register district.

lens.where: fifth-order lens of 1873; the Society's record says the current optic is removed

structures.material: wood tower on blue limestone house
structures.note: 36 ft (11 m) to the centre of the lantern

access.note: Private home since 1936; not open to the public. Do not go onto the property.

facts.agency: Private owner since 1936 (sold by sealed bid)

events.note: Lighthouse Board petitioned Congress for funds for a light here (LighthouseFriends, second-hand)
Appropriation of 15 July 1870 for the light
Contract let; work to wait for a valid title and clearance of a judgment debt
Tower established 1873 (Society's record); work began 1872 after title problems (LighthouseFriends)
Light debuted at the opening of navigation on Lake Champlain
Replaced by a steel skeletal tower with an automatic light
Sold by sealed bid in April 1936; the sale notice in the Ticonderoga Sentinel, as LighthouseFriends quotes it
1950s addition to the house; barn converted to a garage (Society's record gives 1950s)
Within the Camp Dudley Road Historic District; National Register record dated 21 October 1993

keepers.name: James E. Barnes
keepers.note: Civil War veteran who lost a leg at Petersburg (LighthouseFriends). Died 1890 at his sister's home in Fort Ann (LighthouseFriends).

keepers.name: Charles E. Stevens
keepers.note: Veteran; one of the first two keepers who were veterans (LighthouseFriends)

keepers.name: Hans C. Anderssen
keepers.note: LighthouseFriends prints 'Hans Christian Anderssen'. Earlier an assistant keeper at Fire Island (1911). Second wife filed for divorce in 1912 (LighthouseFriends, from 1911-12 newspapers). Ended his career at Cumberland Head in 1941 (LighthouseFriends).

notes_for_editor: (1) Position: the record's coordinates (44.154353, -73.404414) agree with Wikipedia and LighthouseFriends; the Society's point (44 15.43, 73 40.45 printed; roster reads 44.2572, -73.6742) is 24 km away and is set aside. (2) Roster identity: the roster matched by name and position; LighthouseFriends' keeper list agrees with the Society's (LighthouseFriends prints 'Hans Christian Anderssen'). (3) Tower and house: the Society says the light is an octagonal tower 36 ft above a house; LighthouseFriends says 'two-story structure with a Mansard roof and an integrated tower'; Rowlett says a wood tower on a two-story limestone base. The story says two-story house with octagonal tower. (4) Second-hand from LighthouseFriends, not verified in a primary source: the 1868 Board petition, the 1911 newspaper items on Anderssen (Fire Island, marriage, divorce), the 1936 sale notice (quoted as printed), the 1890 death at Fort Ann and the Civil War wound. The Ticonderoga Sentinel is cited as quoted by LighthouseFriends. (5) Treasury 1871 and 1874 are cited by item number; printed pages were not read. (6) NRHP nomination PDF (NRIS 93001136) is a 22 KB not-digitised placeholder; the listing record was read. (7) Not used: Wikipedia's claim that the Lighthouse Board requested the light in 1868 and that the light was 36 ft (11 m) with a 'square house'; Wikipedia is a lead only. (8) Several Westport and Lake Champlain newspaper searches for Barber's Point produced only unrelated hits (including Barbers Point, Hawaii); no newspaper evidence for this station is cited. Do not confuse with Barbers Point Light on Oahu, Hawaii (the commissioner reports' entries refer to Hawaii). (9) Anderssen's private family details are kept to what the sources print; his second wife is not named. (10) No storm, wreck or rescue at this station was found in sources read; that chapter is omitted. (11) Fact check 2026-10-28: the range_nm correction (7.0 to 12.6) is withdrawn. LighthouseFriends gives the light's range as '14 and a half miles' with no unit, so no nautical figure is supported. The story's Bluff Point reference is to Valcour Island, not a 'nearby' station; the distance is not given in the sources read.
